name: Architecture diagram (16:9)
note: Specification approved by the brand team on 2026-10-14. Sizes are the design system's own text styles chosen per density (not the Text Roles modes); spacing, radius and colours are tokens. Icons come from the Faclon architecture icon library, which the user provides. Zone colour-coding and extra arrow colours are still to define.

header.title: optional, top-left; the user decides whether there is a title and what it says

density.how: Count what the user's content needs, take the densest category any count points to, then check the fit: step down if a label needs more than 2 lines, overlaps a connector or forces a gap below the spacing spec; step up if the larger sizes still fit with every gap intact. Larger is preferred when it fits.

counts.nodes: device or system boxes (title tag + icon)
counts.labels: every text item except the title: tags, device labels, arrow labels, notes

status.when: only when the user marks a flow as a status

arrows.other: Any other arrow colour is used only when the user defines it for that diagram; otherwise the default applies.

icons.source: Faclon architecture icon library, provided by the user
icons.until_provided: Ask the user; do not pick, draw or substitute icons.

guardrails.note: Guidance for whoever designs in this format. user_decides = what is made (the user's call); fixed = do not change; must_not = hard limits; avoid = strong advice; design_direction = how to use the system; claude_decides = how it looks, where the designer has freedom. Every design item cites its basis in the design system.
user_decides: What the architecture shows: the systems, devices, connections and protocols. Nothing is added that the user did not supply.
Whether there is a title, and what it says.
Which labels are shown and what they say; until then they stay placeholders.
The scope: how many sections or zones there are and what each contains; when it is unclear, ask.
Which icons are used, from the Faclon architecture icon library they provide.
Any arrow colour beyond the default, data-flow and status colours.

fixed.text: 48px padding on all four sides (spacing/48); content area 1824 × 984 px, and nothing sits outside it.
Optional title at top-left, the blue logo at top-right, gap/grid between the header and the diagram.
Every diagram is Dense, Medium or Open, chosen by counting nodes, labels and zones and then checking the fit.
Text uses the text style set for its element and density (e.g. node tag: Body/SM, Body/MD or Body/XL Semi Bold), never a raw size.
Spacing uses the tokens in the spacing spec: gap/grid between zones, padding/container inside zones, spacing/12 inside nodes, gaps between nodes by density.
Zones, sub-zones, node boxes, node tags and the platform panel follow the shapes spec (fills, borders, radius, elevation).

must_not.text: Hard rule: never edit or change the user's content (no rewriting, shortening, cutting or adding). If a change seems needed, highlight it, suggest how it could be shown better, and change nothing unless the user approves.
Never let text overflow the canvas padding on any side, or the card, box, zone or node it sits in.
Never set text below 12px, however dense the diagram.
Never add a device, system, connection or protocol that the user did not supply.
Never pick, draw or substitute an icon: icons come from the Faclon architecture icon library; until it is provided, ask the user.
Never give an arrow a colour the user did not define; use the default, data-flow or status arrow.
Never use a colour that is not a design-system token, and never sample or approximate one.
Never use a font other than TASA Orbiter (headings) and Inter (body).
Never put a pill radius on a zone, node box, tag or panel.
Never combine a shadow with a border of 2px or more.

avoid.text: Avoid using the accent colours (accent and accent-2 together) on more than roughly 10–15% of the diagram; it is a highlight, not a palette.
Avoid text/tertiary for labels that matter; at 3.4:1 it is for large or non-essential text only.
Avoid arrows crossing each other or running through a node.

design_direction.text: Build each device as a node box: dashed outline, the title tag on top (brand fill, white text) and the device icon below, with gap/inline between them.
Group devices into zones with a heading above each box; nest sub-zones inside with the brand border.
Show the platform (e.g. I/O Sense) as the one lifted panel: container/elevated with Elevation/Low Raised.
Connections use the default dashed slate arrow; the main data flow uses the solid brand arrow; arrow labels sit spacing/4 from the line.
Show states (online, alarm, offline…) with the five intents and their fixed fill/text pairs, and status arrows only where the user marks them.
If the content is too much for the space, do not squeeze it below the minimum size or cut it: tell the user, and offer options (split across slides or pages, a different layout, a table or chart).

claude_decides: How zones, sub-zones and nodes are arranged, and which way the flow reads.
The density category, within the counting and fit rules.
How connectors are routed so they stay clear.
Visual hierarchy: what is the focal point (e.g. the platform) and what stays quiet.
How repeated parts are shown, e.g. one device with 'up to 16' rather than sixteen copies, when the user's content allows it.
to_define: Zone colour-coding (e.g. by network, area or protocol) beyond the zone and sub-zone styles.
Additional arrow colours and their meanings.
The Faclon architecture icon library (provided by the user).
Whether diagrams carry a legend, and where.

overrides.reason: Architecture labels stay legible at any density.
